newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romanian fuel sales fell by 20 percent in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Romanian fuel sales fell by 20 percent in 1997.

text.p: Romanian petrol and diesel sales fell this year after a steep rise in fuel prices and an overall fall in living standards, the head of the country's state-owned oil company was quoted as saying on Tuesday.
"Consumption of all petroleum products has decreased by 20 percent this year against the same period last year," Vifor Ionita, chairman of Compania Romana de Petrol told the daily Libertatea.

Retailers blamed poor sales on the reformist government's move in February to increase fuel, energy and food prices. Fuel prices rose by 50 percent in February, bringing a litre of premium petrol to 2,900 lei (40 cents).
"Few people can still afford a full tank," a petrol station owner told Libertatea. "Most of our clients ask for 10 or 15 litres (two to three imperial gallons)."

Romania annually produces around 6.7 million tonnes of crude oil but needs to import about double that amount to meet demand and keep its big refining sector running. Government plans call for refineries to be sold off or shut down.
Monthly inflation hit 18.8 percent in February and 30.7 percent in March, but fell to 4.3 percent last month and is expected to settle at two percent by the end of the year.
